finding: No Class A, B or D. Every one of the 16 market-only companies is a correctly identified real company that the manifest does not contain, and none duplicates a manifest entry. The mismatch is therefore NOT an identity defect and NOT a manifest omission: the market runtime publishes a global universe while the validation manifest is a curated North-America-plus-Mexico 100. The defect is that the PRODUCT treated manifest membership as a precondition for knowing what kind of business a company is, so a correctly identified company fell to an implicit UNKNOWN. The manifest is a validation universe, not a knowledge base.
policy: Manifest membership is unchanged: 100 companies, version 1.0.1, no additions, no cohort moves. Profile derivation gains a second, explicitly-labelled source -- the SEC registrant's own SIC classification -- which is authored and regulator-assigned, the same epistemic class as the manifest's business_model_class and equally not an empirical claim. 15 of the 16 carry one.

market_only_rows.why: a real company, correctly identified, that the validation manifest does not contain; the manifest universe is deliberately North America + Mexico and this is not a duplicate of any of its 100 entries
